cards.card_text: He opens BIG, telling the king, “You are the most handsome of men; grace has anointed your lips…” Nobody has EVER opened a poem to me like that, friend!
cards.verse_text: You are the most handsome of men; grace has anointed your lips; therefore God has blessed you forever.
cards.snippet: You are the most handsome of men; grace has anointed your lips; therefore God has blessed you forever.

cards.card_text: A garland of grace A turban of fine linen A royal diadem
cards.verse_text: She will set a garland of grace on your head; she will present you with a crown of beauty.”
cards.snippet: She will set a garland of grace on your head; she will present you with a crown of beauty.”

cards.card_text: Titus, Paul's partner and fellow worker (2 Corinthians 8:23), is the one who got the Corinthians' act of grace started.
cards.verse_text: So we urged Titus to help complete your act of grace, just as he had started it.
cards.snippet: So we urged Titus to help complete your act of grace, just as he had started it.

cards.card_text: Titus already started the Corinthians' act of grace.

cards.snippet: So we urged Titus to help complete your act of grace, just as he had started it.

cards.card_text: Since the Corinthians already excel in so much, Paul tells them to see that they also excel in this grace of ___.
cards.verse_text: But just as you excel in everything—in faith, in speech, in knowledge, in complete earnestness, and in the love we inspired in you—see that you also excel in this grace of giving.
cards.snippet: …the love we inspired in you—see that you also excel in this grace of giving.
